attachments.origin_landmark: posterior surface of the lower sternum and xiphoid process
attachments.insertion_landmark: inner surfaces of the costal cartilages of ribs 2-6

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Lies on the inner chest wall directly behind the internal thoracic vessels, which is why it is the landmark for the transversus thoracis plane block.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe placed transversely on the anterior chest wall, parasternal, over the 3rd-4th costal cartilage (the transversus thoracis muscle plane, TTMP, block level originally described).
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Local anesthetic is injected into the interfascial plane between this muscle and the internal intercostal muscle/costal cartilage, deep to the internal thoracic (internal mammary) vessels which run in that same plane and must be identified and avoided.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Sternum medially, ribs/costal cartilages seen in cross-section, internal thoracic vessels visualized (ideally with color Doppler) running in the plane just superficial to this muscle, between it and the internal intercostals.
structures_at_risk: internal thoracic (internal mammary) artery and vein, which run directly in the injection plane
pleura and underlying lung (pneumothorax), deep to this muscle
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The transversus thoracis muscle plane (TTMP) block anesthetizes the anterior cutaneous branches of the intercostal nerves (T2-T6) as they pierce this muscle, providing analgesia for the anterior chest wall/sternum -- used for cardiac surgery (sternotomy), pectus repair, and internal mammary harvest. No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping specific to this muscle's own belly was found; the injection technique targets the fascial plane at its superficial surface rather than an intramuscular motor point.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Ueshima H, Kitamura A (2015) 'Clinical experiences of ultrasound-guided transversus thoracic muscle plane block', J Clin Anesth 27(5):428-429, doi:10.1016/j.jclinane.2015.03.040 -- original clinical description of the TTMP block
